body:
You can stay the night at {{rooms_france}} of France’s Michelin-starred restaurants: {{roomsHotel_france}} are inside a hotel and {{roomsOwn_france}} are restaurants with rooms of their own. {{rooms3_france}} hold three stars. Dinner, bed and breakfast for two starts at {{roomsCheapPrice_france}} (about {{roomsCheapUsd_france}}) at {{roomsCheapName_france}}. Checked {{checked}}.

France invented the idea. The country’s great restaurants grew up in coaching inns and family hotels on the roads south, and many of the best-known still keep their bedrooms: the Troisgros family outside Roanne, the Pics in Valence, the Marcons in the hills above Saint-Bonnet-le-Froid, Michel Guérard at Eugénie-les-Bains. Most sell dinner and a room together, as a “séjour gastronomique” or “demi-pension”, often for less than the two booked apart. The tables below give, for each restaurant, its hotel or rooms, the lowest room price it publishes and its cheapest stay with dinner, all from its own or its hotel’s website. Prices are per room for two unless they say otherwise, include VAT and service, and change with the date; the local tourist tax is usually added on top. For prices at every starred restaurant in the country, rooms or not, see our page of Michelin star restaurants in France, where “Show › With rooms” picks out these {{rooms_france}}.

Which French hotels have a Michelin star restaurant?

These are the hotels with Michelin star restaurants in France: {{roomsHotel_france}} starred restaurants inside a hotel you can book. They run from the palace hotels of Paris, where the three-star Le Cinq at the Four Seasons George V, Épicure at Le Bristol and Plénitude at Cheval Blanc are a lift ride from your room, to the ski hotels of Courchevel and the seaside hotels of the Riviera, most of which close for part of the year. In the country, the hotel and restaurant are often one family’s house: Le Petit Nice on the rocks in Marseille, Les Prés d’Eugénie in the Landes, the Assiette Champenoise outside Reims, Flocons de Sel in Megève and the Auberge du Vieux Puits in the Corbières all hold three stars and have rooms upstairs or across the garden. The MICHELIN Guide also rates hotels, with Keys rather than stars; the Michelin star hotels in France listed here are the ones whose restaurant holds a star.

{{table:rooms-hotel-france}}

Which Michelin star hotels in Paris have a starred restaurant?

{{roomsHotel_paris}} starred restaurants in Paris are inside a hotel, most of them in the grand hotels of the 1st, 8th and 16th arrondissements. Four hold three stars: Le Cinq, Épicure, Plénitude and Le Gabriel at La Réserve. None of them publishes a dinner-and-room package with a price, so book the room and the table separately, the table first, as it is usually the harder of the two to get. For the restaurants themselves, with their menus and prices, see our page of Michelin star restaurants in Paris.

Which French Michelin star restaurants have rooms?

{{roomsOwn_france}} starred restaurants in France have bedrooms of their own rather than a hotel: a few guest rooms above the dining room, a house across the lane or cottages in the vineyard. Les Morainières in the Bugey, with six rooms in the owners’ guest house a few minutes away, is the only one with three stars. The others are mostly one-star tables in the country, where the rooms are the way to eat a long dinner without driving home: the Auberge Sauvage near Mont-Saint-Michel sells its four rooms only with dinner, and the Auberge du Vert Mont in French Flanders gives every room guest a table. At the other end, La Tour d’Argent in Paris lets a single apartment on its fifth floor, facing Notre-Dame, from €2,400 a night.

{{table:rooms-france}}

Where in France can you stay at a Michelin star restaurant?

Everywhere, but most of all in the east and south. Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes has the most, {{rooms_auvergne_rhone_alpes}}, from Lake Annecy and the Alpine ski resorts to the Lyon countryside, then Provence-Alpes-Côte d’Azur with {{rooms_provence_alpes_cote_d_azur}}, Grand Est with {{rooms_grand_est}} (Alsace and Champagne) and Nouvelle-Aquitaine with {{rooms_nouvelle_aquitaine}}, from Bordeaux’s wine châteaux to the Basque coast. Brittany has {{rooms_brittany}}, many of them by the sea. Normandy has {{rooms_normandy}}, among them Le Jardin des Plumes in Giverny, a short walk from Monet’s garden, the Manoir du Lys in the forest at Bagnoles-de-l’Orne and La Renaissance in Argentan.

How much is a gastronomic weekend at a Michelin star restaurant in France?

{{roomsPack_france}} of the {{rooms_france}} publish a price for a stay with dinner. For a single night for two, with dinner at the starred restaurant and breakfast, half of them cost between €435 and €815 (about $490 to $920). At the low end are midweek offers at one-star country inns, such as {{roomsCheapName_france}} in Alsace at {{roomsCheapPrice_france}} for two and Le Jardin des Plumes at €376. At three stars, Restaurant Marcon’s cheapest starts at €725 for two, the Prés d’Eugénie’s Fugue Étoilée at €1,005, Le Petit Nice’s at €1,140 and the Assiette Champenoise’s at €1,740, with drinks included.

Three things to check before you book. First, which restaurant: several hotels sell half board at their bistro rather than the starred dining room, which the tables leave out unless the starred restaurant is named. Second, which nights: many starred restaurants in France close on Sunday and Monday, and packages are often sold only on the nights the kitchen is open, or only midweek. Third, the season: the ski and seaside hotels close for months at a time, and some country restaurants shut for winter.

What is the cheapest Michelin star restaurant with rooms in France?

For a night with dinner included, {{roomsCheapName_france}} at Marlenheim, west of Strasbourg, at {{roomsCheapPrice_france}} for two midweek. For the room alone, {{roomsFromName_france}} at Charmes-sur-Rhône in the Ardèche starts at {{roomsFromPrice_france}} a night, and several Breton and Alsatian inns let rooms for around €100; dinner is then whatever you choose from the menu. A set lunch is the other cheap way in: see our cheapest Michelin star meals.

How to book a stay at a Michelin star restaurant in France

Book the room first, on the hotel’s or restaurant’s own website or by phone: that is where the dinner packages are sold, and a room often comes with a table held for you. Check what time the table is, as smaller places seat everyone at once. Book early for the restaurants with only a handful of rooms (Atmosphères on Lake Bourget and Ezia in the Basque country have four each) and well ahead for summer weekends in Provence and the Riviera. Many packages are prepaid and can’t be refunded, so read the cancellation terms before you pay, and expect to add the tourist tax, a few euros a person a night, when you leave.
